"Goal/Purpose": "To expand the Panama Canal PIEA to promote sustainable land-use management in the Panama Canal watershed and support implementation of relevant objectives and targets of the Indicative Environmental Land-Use Plan for the Panama Canal Watershed (PIOTA–CHCP).",
"Action/Intervention": "Expanding the Panama Canal PIEA through the PBP Agreement, leveraging the PIEA incentive model for performance-based implementation; providing a package of incentives targeting small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them; fostering conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implementing sustainable agriculture packages, including agro-forestry and silvopastoral systems; supporting family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; and expanding the Conservation PES Programme in the Panama Canal watershed.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Panama Canal watershed, including prioritized forest ecosystems and the basin covered by the PIOTA–CHCP.",
"Target Audience": "Small scale producers and local communities, including equitably women and men among them.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Sustainable land-use management; conservation and restoration of prioritized forest ecosystems; implementation of sustainable agriculture packages, including agro-forestry and silvopastoral systems; support for family agriculture and alternative livelihoods; expansion of the Conservation PES Programme; and support for implementation of relevant objectives and targets of the PIOTA–CHCP related to territorial and environmental management, ecosystems and protected areas, decarbonization, climate resilience, and sustainable land-use in the basin."
panama_CNR_2:

"Action/Intervention": "Develop the institutional and management structure to enable implementation of the PIEA incentives package model outside the Panama Canal watershed; implement activities to develop such institutional and management structure as part of Output 2, aligned with Panama’s REDD+ NS implementation approach and Executive Decree No. 479 of April 23, 2013; use relevant PIOTAs to guide implementation of the PIEA package of incentives; finance the actual implementation of the PIEA package of incentives outside the Panama Canal watershed under a socially inclusive and gender-responsive approach.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Outside the Panama Canal watershed; water basins as the primary units for environmental and territorial planning.",
"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Institutional and management structures are developed to enable implementation of the PIEA incentives package model outside the Panama Canal watershed, and the PIEA package of incentives is implemented outside the Panama Canal watershed under a socially inclusive and gender-responsive approach."
panama_CNR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "To develop the institutional and management structure to implement a socially inclusive and gender-responsive incentives program targeting Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, tailored to their socio-economic characteristics, relationship with forest ecosystems, and traditional knowledge, and linked to measurable outcomes.",
"Action/Intervention": "Implement an incentives Programme for Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendants, and small-scale producers; tailor the programme to the specific socio-economic characteristics of these groups; implement instruments to stimulate the conservation and sustainable management of forests and the management and sustainable use of non-timber forest products; incorporate livelihood activities compatible with protected area management, including community nurseries for native seedlings, value chains for non-timber forest products such as honey, seeds, fibers, and handicrafts, and low-impact ecotourism activities such as guiding, trails, and signage; align all activities with protected area zoning and management plans; design and implement the programme following the PBP logic, linking payments to measurable outcomes.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Forest ecosystems, protected areas, and non-timber forest product management and use.",
"Target Audience": "Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendant communities, and small-scale producers, including women and men among them.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Conservation and sustainable management of forests; sustainable use of non-timber forest products; promotion of conservation efforts through livelihood activities compatible with protected area management; environmental integrity and sustainability; payments linked to measurable outcomes."
panama_CNR_4:

"Action/Intervention": "Financing the National Restoration Programme; enriching secondary forests; promoting native regeneration and reforestation with native species; fostering ecosystem connectivity through biological corridors; increasing nursery production; enhancing carbon stocks through ecological restoration in protected areas and their buffer zones; strengthening effective management in protected areas and their buffer zones; improving landscape connectivity by establishing biological corridors; promoting Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in buffer zones; aligning all interventions with protected area zoning and management plans.",

"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified in the target.",

panama_CNR_5:

"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, ACP, firefighters, other relevant institutions, and local communities, such as Indigenous Peoples, Afro Descendants and local communities, including equitably women and men among them.",

panama_HR_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "Define, prioritize, implement, track, adjust, and consolidate a portfolio of sectoral mitigation policies and measures to reduce GHG emissions, using up-to-date GHG projections as a reference, and ensure their continuity beyond 2035.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define a prioritized portfolio of policies and measures by sector, with institutional leads, time horizon, and indicative contribution to GHG reduction; strengthen the use of the ReNAM within the National Climate Transparency Platform for registration and tracking of mitigation actions through technical guidelines, accompaniment, and inter-institutional coordination agreements; analyze the technical, institutional, and economic feasibility of the main mitigation measures identified; establish formal mechanisms of inter-institutional coordination for mitigation implementation; implement pilot mitigation projects and programs in prioritized sectors (energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes); formalize implementation agreements with sectoral entities and key actors; technically accompany sectoral entities for the launch of prioritized mitigation measures; activate existing or under-development economic and financial instruments to support execution of viable mitigation measures; adjust the mitigation-measures portfolio based on observed results; adjust economic incentives, institutional arrangements, and technical guidelines that facilitate sustained adoption of scalable mitigation measures, in coordination with Target 14; strengthen coherence between mitigation, sectoral planning, and territorial planning so that new public and private investments consider GHG-reduction criteria; review the national emissions-reduction trajectory against the required trajectory to identify gaps and guide corrective decisions; reinforce inter-institutional coordination to close gaps; consolidate implemented mitigation measures within permanent instruments of sectoral and climate planning.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate mitigation; sectoral and territorial planning; National Climate Transparency Platform; ReNAM; prioritized sectors: energy, waste, agriculture, and industrial processes.",
"Target Audience": "Sectoral entities involved in mitigation implementation, institutional leads, key actors, inter-institutional coordination bodies, and public and private investment actors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A prioritized and feasible mitigation-measures portfolio with defined institutional leads, time horizons, and indicative GHG-reduction contributions; strengthened national registration and tracking of mitigation actions through ReNAM; pilot mitigation projects launched in prioritized sectors; formalized implementation commitments and coordination mechanisms; activated economic and financial support instruments; adjusted incentives, institutional arrangements, and technical guidelines for sustained adoption of scalable mitigation measures; improved coherence between mitigation and sectoral and territorial planning; identification of gaps in the national emissions-reduction trajectory and corrective action; continuity of mitigation measures beyond 2035."
panama_HR_2:
"Goal/Purpose": "Update and execute the National Forest Restoration Program at scale, with validated baselines, corridor-based prioritization, effective-conservation arrangements, productive restoration in agricultural landscapes, zero unplanned agricultural expansion causing forest conversion within corridors, traceability of restoration actions, mangrove restoration, and verifiable LULUCF accounting.",
"Action/Intervention": "Validate a national baseline quantifying and characterizing restorable degraded areas, areas to be placed under effective conservation, and farms/agricultural landscapes eligible for productive restoration; disaggregate the target into quantitative pathways of 100,000 ha total, 2,500 ha mangrove, and 25,000 ha agricultural, defining gaps, priority territories, and preliminary annual targets by type; delimit and validate the Azuero, Coclé, and Veraguas corridors, approve functional zoning, and define land-use rules and intervention priorities; define effective-conservation guidelines for restored areas including conservation agreements with landowners, community co-management where applicable, surveillance and compliance mechanisms, and management leads, and integrate these into SINAP/OECM as appropriate or equivalent conservation arrangements in productive landscapes; reorient agricultural programs and incentives to implement silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms, with productive-performance targets of at least 20% productivity increase and eligibility criteria linked to corridor zoning and non-conversion of forests; define and launch an operational mechanism to eliminate unplanned agricultural expansion implying forest conversion within corridors through municipal land-use planning and zoning guidelines, land-use-change traceability with satellite monitoring, and inter-institutionally coordinated control and compliance measures; design, implement, and monitor a traceability system for restoration actions aligned with existing national systems and national/international reporting requirements; approve an intervention plan for restoration of 2,500 ha of mangrove including site selection, permits, agreements with communities/users, technical execution, and post-restoration protection and monitoring; execute the program with explicit annual targets toward 100,000 ha total, 2,500 ha mangrove, and 25,000 ha agricultural, prioritizing interventions by corridor and ensuring each intervention has an associated effective-conservation instrument; implement silvopastoral/agroforestry systems through agricultural extension with technical assistance, access to inputs, and productive follow-up to achieve the 20% productivity increase with agreed indicators; operationalize the zero-unplanned-expansion mechanism through periodic land-cover-change monitoring, territorial early warnings, coordinated corrective measures, and semi-annual reports by corridor with public/administrative traceability; strengthen and evaluate conservation arrangements to reduce reversal risks in restored areas and adjust incentives and management rules according to corridor performance; adjust the restoration portfolio to prioritize interventions with greater carbon performance and permanence, ensuring verifiable LULUCF accounting consistent with the national reporting system; carry out verification across hectares restored by type, demonstrable effective conservation, productivity increase on intervened farms, compliance with zero unplanned expansion in corridors, and LULUCF accounting of at least 1 million tCO2e.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "National forest restoration program areas; restorable degraded areas; areas to be placed under effective conservation; farms and agricultural landscapes eligible for productive restoration; the Azuero, Coclé, and Veraguas corridors; restored areas in productive landscapes; mangroves; forests within corridors; land-use and land-cover monitoring systems; LULUCF reporting domain.",
"Target Audience": "National Forest Restoration Program implementers; landowners; communities/users; management leads; agricultural programs and extension services; prioritized farms; municipalities; inter-institutional authorities responsible for control, compliance, monitoring, zoning, conservation arrangements, and national reporting systems.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated national baseline and corridor zoning; quantified pathways and annual targets for 100,000 ha total restoration, including 2,500 ha of mangrove and 25,000 ha in agricultural landscapes; approved and implemented effective-conservation instruments for restored areas; implementation of silvopastoral and agroforestry systems on prioritized farms with at least a 20% productivity increase; an operational mechanism eliminating unplanned agricultural expansion that causes forest conversion within corridors; a functioning traceability and monitoring system for restoration actions and land-cover change; strengthened conservation arrangements reducing reversal risks; restoration portfolio adjusted for greater carbon performance and permanence; verification of hectares restored by type, effective conservation, farm productivity gains, compliance with zero unplanned expansion, and LULUCF accounting of at least 1 million tCO2e."
panama_HR_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "Ensure minimum standards of effective conservation through the review and update of the regulatory, normative, and operational framework of SINAP; expand SINAP to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine; strengthen effective conservation inside and outside formal protected areas through OECM and complementary arrangements; align the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) with the Nature Pledge; develop integrated management in 10 strategic watersheds; secure permanent financing, monitoring, governance coherence, and long-term incorporation of effective management into national planning instruments.",
"Action/Intervention": "Review and update the regulatory, normative, and operational framework of SINAP; carry out a national diagnosis of effective management of terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas, identifying gaps in planning, financing, personnel, control, monitoring, and community participation; define a technical roadmap for SINAP expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine, prioritizing areas of high ecological value, connectivity, and climate resilience and incorporating effective-management feasibility and sustainable financing criteria; identify, evaluate, and recognize OECM and complementary arrangements in indigenous, private, and community territories and integrate them into the national conservation system; update and align the NBSAP with the Nature Pledge's governance, financing, incentives, and information-management frameworks; select and prioritize 10 strategic watersheds for integrated management plans; strengthen SINAP's operational capacities through investment in personnel, equipment, control and surveillance, and co-management mechanisms; develop, approve, and implement integrated management plans in the 10 priority watersheds with zoning, control mechanisms, community participation, and alignment with municipal and sectoral plans; channel permanent financing for SINAP management through the Fondo Panamá Natural and other mechanisms; periodically evaluate management effectiveness of protected areas and OECM using ecological, social, and governance indicators and adjust management plans, institutional arrangements, and resource allocation according to results; guarantee articulation among SINAP, indigenous territories, and local governments; verify compliance with coverage goals and effective management, including ecological performance, governance, and financial sustainability; incorporate effective management of SINAP and OECM permanently into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "SINAP (National System of Protected Areas); terrestrial, marine, and continental protected areas; Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures (OECM); indigenous, private, and community territories; 10 strategic watersheds; areas of high ecological value, connectivity, and climate resilience; national conservation system; national, budgetary, and sectoral planning instruments.",
"Target Audience": "SINAP; protected areas and OECM managers; indigenous territories; private and community territories; local governments; municipal and sectoral planning authorities; Fondo Panamá Natural; institutions responsible for the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP); communities participating in watershed and conservation management.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Minimum standards of effective conservation established; national diagnosis of management gaps completed; technical roadmap for expansion to 40% terrestrial and 60% marine defined; OECM and complementary arrangements recognized and integrated into the national conservation system; NBSAP updated and aligned with the Nature Pledge; 10 strategic watersheds selected and integrated management plans developed, approved, and implemented; strengthened operational capacities of SINAP; permanent financing secured for operation, monitoring, and compliance; periodic evaluation of ecological, social, and governance effectiveness conducted with resulting management adjustments; coherence ensured among conservation, land-use planning, local development, and cultural safeguards; compliance verified for coverage goals, ecological performance, governance, and financial sustainability; effective management of SINAP and OECM incorporated permanently into national, budgetary, and sectoral planning beyond 2035."
panama_HR_4:
"Goal/Purpose": "Conserve priority native species and manage human-wildlife conflicts through updated prioritization, identification of critical conflict areas, implementation of management measures, institutional strengthening, monitoring, territorial scaling, formalized protocols, operational integration, and permanent updating mechanisms.",
"Action/Intervention": "Update and validate a national list of priority native species for conservation using criteria of extinction risk, ecological value, territorial distribution, and level of human-wildlife conflict, with focus on species whose loss would have systemic effects; identify and delimit five critical areas of human-wildlife conflict and analyze causes, actors involved, socio-economic impacts, and existing institutional capacities; implement conflict-management measures in prioritized critical areas, including prevention protocols, compensation, risk management, and strengthening local capacities for coexistence; review the institutional base and verify the need to establish a monitoring system for priority species and human-wildlife conflicts, integrating indicators of population status, genetic diversity, and reduction of incidents, interoperable with national environmental information systems; scale up species-management and human-wildlife coexistence approaches to new priority territories, strengthening articulation with SINAP management plans, biological corridors, and productive landscapes; formalize national protocols through administrative and technical instruments of MiAMBIENTE for management of priority species and human-wildlife conflicts, defining institutional responsibilities, activation criteria, inter-institutional coordination mechanisms, and territorial application guidelines; integrate conservation and conflict-management programs into the regular operational plans of SINAP and the biodiversity and wildlife directorates, ensuring annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; establish a permanent mechanism for updating priority species and critical conflict areas based on scientific evidence and continuous monitoring.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Native species conservation, human-wildlife conflict management, priority territories, critical conflict areas, SINAP management plans, biological corridors, productive landscapes, and national environmental information systems.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, SINAP, the biodiversity and wildlife directorates, institutions involved in inter-institutional coordination, and local capacities in prioritized critical areas and new priority territories.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A validated national list of priority native species; identification and delimitation of five critical human-wildlife conflict areas; implementation of prevention, compensation, risk-management, and coexistence measures in prioritized areas; verification of the need for a monitoring system with indicators on population status, genetic diversity, and incident reduction; scaled-up species-management and coexistence approaches in new priority territories; formalized national protocols with defined institutional responsibilities and coordination mechanisms; integration of programs into regular operational plans with annual planning, recurrent budget allocation, and continuous technical follow-up; and a permanent evidence-based mechanism for periodic updating of priority species and critical conflict areas."
panama_HR_5:
"Goal/Purpose": "Control illegal wildlife trafficking in prioritized regions of the country through coordinated inter-institutional action, strengthened legal and sustainable trade controls, integration of information systems, evaluation and adjustment of mechanisms, and stable allocation of operational resources, while incorporating conservation and zoonotic-risk criteria.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify and prioritize at least five regions with high incidence of illegal wildlife trafficking; establish inter-institutional operational coordination protocols among MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, Customs, and security agencies; train park rangers, health personnel, and security forces in species identification, safe handling of seized wildlife, and zoonotic-risk prevention; implement coordinated and permanent control operations in prioritized regions; strengthen control mechanisms for legal and sustainable trade of species through traceability, permit compliance, and respect for traditional uses of indigenous peoples and local communities; integrate operational and control information into national environmental and risk-information systems; evaluate effectiveness of control mechanisms and inter-institutional coordination and identify gaps; adjust protocols, administrative procedures, and regulatory frameworks based on lessons learned and newly identified threats; define and ensure a stable scheme for allocating human, logistical, and operational resources through institutional budgets and regular operational plans; consolidate a national interoperable system for registration, analysis, and follow-up of illegal wildlife trafficking cases and zoonotic-risk events.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Wildlife trafficking control; legal and sustainable trade of species; environmental, health, customs, and security sectors; prioritized regions of the country; critical points of extraction, transport, and commercialization; national environmental, risk, health, and security information systems.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MINSA, Customs, security agencies, park rangers, health personnel, security forces, indigenous peoples and local communities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least five high-incidence regions prioritized; inter-institutional coordination protocols established; field and control personnel trained; coordinated and permanent control operations implemented in prioritized regions; strengthened traceability and permit compliance for legal and sustainable species trade with respect for traditional uses; operational and control information integrated into national systems; effectiveness of control mechanisms and coordination evaluated and gaps identified; protocols, procedures, and regulatory frameworks adjusted; stable human, logistical, and operational resource allocation integrated into institutional budgets and plans; a national interoperable system established to monitor trends, routes, zoonotic-risk events, and effectiveness of control measures."
panama_HR_6:
"Goal/Purpose": "Identify and prioritize the main pathways for the introduction of invasive alien species at the national level; define inter-institutional coordination on invasive alien species; strengthen biosecurity and prevention controls at critical entry points; implement early-detection and rapid-warning systems; develop and execute early-response plans; and integrate generated information into national environmental and risk-information systems to allow evaluation of reductions in the rate of introduction and establishment.",
"Action/Intervention": "Use existing information from MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, Customs, and ARAP to identify and prioritize introduction pathways for invasive alien species; define a basic scheme for inter-institutional coordination articulated with existing mechanisms for plant health, animal health, and environmental control, without creating new bodies during this phase; strengthen biosecurity and prevention controls at ports, airports, and prioritized borders using environmental- and health-risk criteria; implement early-detection and rapid-warning systems for priority invasive alien species in protected areas, productive zones, and aquatic ecosystems using existing monitoring and surveillance capacities; develop and execute early-response plans including containment, control, or eradication measures depending on species type and territorial context; integrate information from controls and responses into national environmental and risk-information systems.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "National level; critical entry points into the country (ports, airports, and prioritized borders); protected areas; productive zones; aquatic ecosystems; plant health, animal health, and environmental control.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE, MIDA, Customs, ARAP, and institutions involved in plant health, animal health, environmental control, monitoring, surveillance, and national environmental and risk-information systems.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Main pathways for the introduction of invasive alien species are identified and prioritized; a basic inter-institutional coordination scheme is defined; biosecurity and prevention controls at critical entry points are strengthened; early-detection and rapid-warning systems are implemented for priority invasive alien species; early-response plans are developed and executed; information from controls and responses is integrated into national environmental and risk-information systems; and reductions in the rate of introduction and establishment can be evaluated."
panama_HR_7:
"Goal/Purpose": "By 2035, Panama will reduce pollution and its cumulative effects by reducing by at least 50% the excess nutrients released into the environment and the risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals, complemented by a significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors.",
"Action/Intervention": "Prioritize a limited set of watersheds and critical territories where pollution by nutrients and chemicals represents greater environmental, health, or economic risks; identify the national technological gap for the reduction of pollution by chemicals and nutrients and map clean technologies available internationally that are not yet present or widespread in Panama; define a national pathway for the progressive reduction of risks from chemicals and nutrients, with clear milestones at 2030 and 2035, identifying priority sectors, types of instruments to be used, and expected levels of intervention, without yet initiating implementation at the national scale; align the chemicals- and nutrients-reduction pathway with the analysis of perverse and positive incentives in Target 14, identifying polluting practices currently incentivized and technical alternatives that require economic or other incentives for their adoption; design very focused pilot interventions in one or two prioritized territories to test combinations of technical assistance, incentive adjustments, and institutional arrangements for the reduction of pollutant loads; implement integrated territorial interventions in the prioritized watersheds and productive zones, combining the progressive reduction of the use of polluting inputs, integrated nutrient management, and the adoption of practices and technologies of lower environmental impact; technically accompany producers, agro-industries, and industrial actors in the transition toward less polluting productive practices; apply in the intervened territories the economic incentives and technical support prioritized under Target 14; scale up the adoption of clean technologies and low-impact nutrient-management practices to new territories and productive sectors, prioritizing those with the greatest contribution to pollution and with demonstrated enabling conditions; focus additional actions on the territories or sectors that still present elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients, reinforcing combinations of clean technologies, incentives, and environmental control.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Watersheds and critical territories; marine-coastal, adaptation, and restoration-prioritized territories; prioritized watersheds and productive zones; new territories and productive sectors; sectors and territories with elevated levels of pollution by chemicals and nutrients.",
"Target Audience": "Panama; producers; agro-industries; industrial actors.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "At least 50% reduction in excess nutrients released into the environment by 2035; reduced risks associated with the use of pesticides, fungicides, and hazardous chemicals; significant increase in the adoption of clean technologies in productive sectors; progressive reduction of pollutant loads; adoption of low-impact nutrient-management practices and cleaner alternatives in prioritized and additional territories and sectors."
panama_HR_8:
"Goal/Purpose": "Prioritize wild species amenable to sustainable management at the national level, develop and implement sustainable-management schemes for those species, and ensure coherence with conservation objectives, ecological limits, and sectoral policies.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define technical, social, and territorial criteria for national prioritization of wild species; identify and validate a preliminary list of priority species in coordination with scientific authorities, indigenous peoples, and local communities; design and launch pilot management plans including use guidelines, population monitoring, traceability, and benefit-sharing in selected territories; strengthen technical and organizational capacities of local communities and indigenous peoples for management, transformation, and commercialization of products and services derived from sustainable management of wild species; implement control and follow-up mechanisms to ensure use within sustainable ecological limits and coherence with measures for control of illegal trafficking; evaluate results of pilot plans to identify species, territories, and models with greater ecological, social, and economic viability; integrate sustainable-management schemes for wild species into sectoral policies on biodiversity, tourism, and rural development, ensuring regulatory and technical coherence.",

panama_HR_9:
"Goal/Purpose": "Update, harmonize, and strengthen Panama’s legal, administrative, policy, and institutional frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing; ensure continuous participation of indigenous peoples and local communities in governance; and implement monitoring and reporting mechanisms to guarantee compliance with the Nagoya Protocol and the Cali Fund.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out a comparative legal analysis on frameworks for access to genetic resources, DSI, and benefit-sharing, incorporating the most recent decisions of the CBD, the Nagoya Protocol, and the Cali Fund; identify existing legal, administrative, and policy frameworks in Panama that require updating or harmonization to incorporate DSI, FPIC, and benefit-sharing mechanisms; evaluate the actual functioning of the existing system for access to genetic resources through review of contracts, agreed and delivered benefits, processing times, and compliance with FPIC in previous experiences; design national FPIC guidelines in a participatory manner and considering gender equity, in coordination with indigenous peoples and local communities, ensuring coherence with international standards and the Panamanian constitutional framework; strengthen technical and institutional capacities in competent entities for management of access to genetic resources, compliance monitoring, and benefit negotiation; approve a legal and administrative framework that establishes the mandatory procedure for reviewing new laws and policies, creates the National Registry of Applications and Contracts, defines the benefit-sharing mechanism, adopts official contract templates, and establishes periodic compliance audits with mandatory application from 2028 onward; institutionalize permanent dialogue processes with indigenous peoples and local communities; establish clear procedures for benefit management, including agreements, funds, or redistribution mechanisms; implement national monitoring and reporting mechanisms.",

"Goal/Purpose": "To exhaustively review incentives and subsidies with direct or indirect impact on biodiversity; adopt an official methodology to evaluate biodiversity impacts and classify incentives as harmful, neutral, or positive; evaluate and prioritize the most critical harmful incentives; design and implement an incentives-reform roadmap; redirect resources toward positive incentives for biodiversity; increase the volume and scope of positive incentives; integrate biodiversity criteria into new incentives and subsidies; and publish and periodically update the inventory and status of incentives to ensure transparency and follow-up.",

"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Priority climate variables are defined for epidemiological surveillance; a national methodology for climate-information integration is established; climate variables and projections are incorporated into prioritized health facilities' surveillance systems with interoperability ensured; health personnel are trained, especially in highly vulnerable regions; sectoral protocols are formalized for preventive measures, contingency plans, and coordination; climate-health integration is expanded with methodological consistency and data quality in at least 80% of health facilities; climate-sensitive health indicators are periodically reported in national adaptation and loss-and-damage monitoring systems; evaluation results are incorporated into updated sectoral health and adaptation plans, ensuring continuity and improvement beyond 2030."
panama_HR_25:
"Goal/Purpose": "Strengthen and operationalize climate adaptation and Loss and Damage monitoring, evaluation, data governance, interoperability, reporting, and regulatory/procedural frameworks for decision-making and transparency.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize institutional agreements on data flow per indicator, including leads, periodicity, format, validation, and technical focal points, prioritizing indicators with yellow/red traffic-light status and those most used in public decision-making; develop the draft regulatory framework for the Planned Relocation protocol; install a universal data-collection scheme with field templates and an interoperable repository to reduce duplication and standardize climate-change and Loss and Damage variables; finalize the Loss and Damage section in the National Climate Transparency Platform (PNTC); design the climate-displacement component, including cooperation and data-flow agreements, event typology, minimum variables, and reporting pathway; evaluate the functionality of the Adaptation Monitoring & Evaluation system and the Loss and Damage subsystem with external technical cooperation through gap analysis, interoperability, roles, sustainability, and costs; improve data source and quality through cleansing of series, validation rules, quality control, and an annual recalculation cycle with data providers; issue or adopt the Ministerial Resolution on technical aspects, or ensure its effective implementation through manuals, leads, schedule, and institutional compliance; operate the M&E Module in the PNTC with recalculation executed by data providers through an annual calendar, cross-validation, and publication; achieve interoperability with the Risk Observatory through a shared data dictionary, API/ETL, and a joint risk–measures–results–L&D dashboard; implement pilot projects to evaluate the effectiveness of measures versus the quantification of Loss and Damage by sector or territory, including equipment and evaluation methodology; operationalize the Planned Relocation Protocol through last alternative criteria, pathway of rights, livelihoods and services, institutional roles, and financing mechanisms; publish the annual M&E dashboard covering adaptation and Loss and Damage with updated information for decision-making and transparency.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate change adaptation, Loss and Damage, climate displacement, planned relocation, national climate transparency and monitoring systems, and risk information systems.",
"Target Audience": "Institutions responsible for indicator data flows, data providers, institutions required to comply with the Ministerial Resolution, the National Climate Transparency Platform (PNTC), the Adaptation M&E system, the Loss and Damage subsystem, the Risk Observatory, external technical cooperation actors, and public decision-makers.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Institutionalized data-flow arrangements per indicator; a draft regulatory framework and operational procedure for Planned Relocation; a universal and interoperable data-collection and repository scheme; a finalized Loss and Damage section in the PNTC; a designed climate-displacement component with defined agreements, typology, variables, and reporting pathway; an evaluated Adaptation M&E system and Loss and Damage subsystem with identified gaps, interoperability, roles, sustainability, and costs; improved data quality through cleansing, validation, quality control, and annual recalculation; issuance, adoption, or effective implementation of the Ministerial Resolution on technical aspects; operation of the PNTC M&E Module with recalculation by data providers, cross-validation, and publication; interoperability with the Risk Observatory and a joint dashboard; pilot evaluations of measure effectiveness versus Loss and Damage quantification; and annual publication of an updated adaptation and Loss and Damage dashboard for decision-making and transparency."
panama_HR_26:
"Goal/Purpose": "Formally establish and operationalize a National Integrated Marine-Coastal and Wetlands Monitoring System to integrate monitoring efforts, avoid duplication, generate standardized national information and baselines for seagrass, coral reefs, wetlands, sea turtles, and marine water quality, and ensure its use in marine-coastal planning, conservation, management of the marine SINAP, and climate-change adaptation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Constitute the system through an administrative instrument defining objectives, mandatory components, institutional roles, data flow and custody, minimum standards, reporting frequency, and annual operations; carry out and consolidate a national inventory of existing monitoring initiatives and databases; adopt standardized national protocols and an integrated sampling design; design the National Marine Water Quality Index; generate preliminary national cartography of seagrass and coral reefs with field validation; define the methodology and structure of the National Wetlands Inventory; design the National Sea Turtle Monitoring System; put into operation the system's National Platform with repository, dashboards, and reports; complete and publish the official National Map of Seagrass and Coral Reefs and establish sentinel sites; update and publish the official National Wetlands Inventory and implement periodic monitoring; implement the National Sea Turtle Monitoring System with a standardized database and management measures linked to fisheries regulation and control; implement the National Marine Water Quality Index through monitoring campaigns in priority coastal zones and marine SINAP areas; ensure permanent financing for technical personnel, field campaigns, laboratory analysis, platform, and reporting through public budget and national environmental financial mechanisms.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Marine-coastal and wetlands monitoring, including seagrass, coral reefs, coastal and continental wetlands, sea turtles, marine water quality, priority coastal zones, and areas of the marine SINAP.",
"Target Audience": "MiAMBIENTE; governmental, academic, and NGO entities involved in marine-coastal and wetlands monitoring; decision-makers; marine-coastal planning authorities; marine SINAP managers; fisheries management and control authorities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A formally constituted and financed national monitoring system with standardized protocols, integrated sampling design, interoperable national information platform, official repository, indicator dashboards, periodic reports, a national inventory of initiatives and databases, a National Marine Water Quality Index, preliminary and official national cartography of seagrass and coral reefs, a national network of sentinel sites, an official National Wetlands Inventory with periodic monitoring, an operational National Sea Turtle Monitoring System with a standardized database and management measures in critical zones, and monitoring results integrated into planning, conservation, fisheries management, and climate adaptation decisions."
panama_HR_27:
"Goal/Purpose": "Regulate and operationalize the Climate Risk Observatory at the national level and establish, pilot, scale up, and consolidate a territorial network of observatories/units and early meteorological warning systems that support climate-risk-informed territorial planning, adaptation project accompaniment, and standardized reporting into the national M&E system.",
"Action/Intervention": "Define the Observatory architecture, including components, tools, dashboards, data standards, institutional roles, access rules, updating protocols, and the official set of adaptation, loss, and damage indicators aligned with Target 25; design the operational model with minimum services, protocols for accompanying local governments, criteria for territorial prioritization, and a standard package of tools; constitute the Community Resilience Technical Team and define coordination with universities, CSOs, municipalities, and community councils; formalize territorial alliances through framework agreements for hosting and operating observatories; design the territorial Network of Early Meteorological Warning Systems in coordination with IMHPA and SINAPROC, including priority municipalities/watersheds, activation and response protocols, communication channels, and interoperability and coverage requirements; agree with ASEP and mobile-telephony operators on interoperability and mass-diffusion of warnings, including free messages and immediate emission mechanisms in high-risk zones; implement pilot observatories in prioritized regions with a technical focal point, annual work plan, local attention mechanism, and capacity to accompany adaptation projects including NbS; operate early-warning systems in pilot territories with simulation exercises, community-communication protocols, and feedback mechanisms; integrate climate analysis into territorial planning and local investment prioritization with support from observatories and national guidelines linked to Target 22; systematize and report territorial information on resilience, vulnerability, and implemented measures using standardized formats and quality verification for the Climate Risk Observatory and Target 25; adjust the model based on pilot evaluation and document costs, capacities, barriers, and lessons learned for 2031-2033 scale-up; scale up the observatory network to new regions using consistent standards and coordination pathways; consolidate a continuous territorial capacity-strengthening program with standardized curricula and alliances with universities/NGOs; strengthen technical and operational interoperability between territorial observatories and the Climate Risk Observatory through improved automation of data flows, dashboards, and comparative territorial analysis; integrate the territorial network into planning and financing mechanisms so projects and investments use observatory technical assistance and report results through the national M&E system; ensure the verifiable operation of at least 10 observatories/units with minimum standards.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate risk management, territorial planning, adaptation, loss and damage monitoring, resilience, early meteorological warning systems, municipal and watershed-level governance, and nature-based solutions.",
"Target Audience": "Climate Risk Observatory; territorial observatories/units; local governments; municipalities; community councils; universities; CSOs; local actors; IMHPA; SINAPROC; ASEP; mobile-telephony operators; prioritized territories/regions; communities.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A nationally regulated and operational Climate Risk Observatory with standardized architecture, indicators, and reporting pathways; operational territorial observatories/units and municipal/watershed early-warning systems in prioritized and scaled-up regions; strengthened territorial capacities through technical assistance, training, and alliances; climate risk integrated into district plans and local investment prioritization; standardized territorial information feeding the national Observatory and M&E system with periodic quality verification; improved interoperability, automation, dashboards, and comparative territorial analysis for national decisions and financing; documented pilot lessons for 2031-2033 scale-up; and verifiable operation of at least 10 observatories/units meeting minimum standards, including active technical assistance, support for adaptation projects, operational EWS, integration into territorial planning, and periodic reporting to the national Observatory."
panama_HR_28:
"Goal/Purpose": "To formalize and operationalize the financial architecture of the Nature Pledge, strengthen the management and coordination of the Fondo Panamá Natural and the Fondo Reforesta, align financing with climate, biodiversity, and land targets, and guarantee stable, transparent, and long-term financing for prioritized actions in restoration, conservation, territorial adaptation, and mitigation.",
"Action/Intervention": "Formalize the financial architecture of the Nature Pledge; define the role of the Fondo Panamá Natural, the Fondo Reforesta, and other financial vehicles; define governance mechanisms, eligibility criteria, and alignment with climate, biodiversity, and land targets; strengthen institutional capacities for trust fund management, capital mobilization, and financial administration; review and update the operating regulations of the Fondo Reforesta; simplify processes, clarify roles, update eligibility requirements, reduce procedures, and establish maximum evaluation and disbursement timeframes; approve the final version of the Conservation and Community Development Plan of the Fondo Panamá Natural; develop a national portfolio of reforestation, restoration, and agroforestry projects aligned with priority regions, degraded areas, and implementing actors; design and approve the governance model of the Fondo Panamá Natural; prepare and formalize the legal agreement of the Fondo Panamá Natural; establish a permanent technical team to support project formulation, follow-up, and evaluation under the Fondo Reforesta and strengthen capacities of implementing actors; align existing fiscal and financial incentives with the Nature Pledge architecture and Target 14 incentives reform; establish social, environmental, and gender safeguards; capitalize and put into full operation the Fondo Panamá Natural and the Fondo Reforesta; mobilize at least USD 300 million toward prioritized actions; implement innovative financing mechanisms including PES, biodiversity credits, and carbon markets with monitoring, reporting, and verification systems; publish periodic reports of financing and impacts.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Nature finance, biodiversity, climate, land, restoration, reforestation, agroforestry, protected areas, degraded areas, territorial adaptation, mitigation, and the National System of Protected Areas.",
"Target Audience": "Fondo Panamá Natural, Fondo Reforesta, implementing actors in territory, local communities, indigenous peoples, vulnerable groups, investors, civil society, and institutions responsible for trust fund management, capital mobilization, financial administration, and incentives coordination.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A formalized and coordinated financial architecture for the Nature Pledge; updated and simplified operating regulations for the Fondo Reforesta; an approved Conservation and Community Development Plan for the Fondo Panamá Natural; an approved governance model and formalized legal agreement for the Fondo Panamá Natural; a national portfolio of reforestation, restoration, and agroforestry projects; a permanent technical support team for financed projects; aligned fiscal and financial incentives; established social, environmental, and gender safeguards; the capitalization and full operation of the Fondo Panamá Natural and the Fondo Reforesta; stable financial flows from public, private, and international cooperation sources; mobilization of at least USD 300 million; implementation of PES, biodiversity credits, and carbon markets with monitoring, reporting, and verification systems; and periodic financing and impact reports ensuring transparency, accountability, and trust."
panama_HR_29:
"Goal/Purpose": "To harmonize the national Roadmap for implementation of the Escazú Agreement with the Nature Pledge governance framework; design and implement a national mechanism for the protection of environmental defenders; integrate access-to-environmental-information principles into national information and monitoring systems; develop and implement operational protocols and territorial mechanisms for public participation and access to environmental justice in Nature Pledge implementation; define indicators on access to information, participation, protection of defenders, and gender equity; incorporate equitable representation and a gender approach into Nature Pledge decision-making spaces; and consolidate local capacities for mediation, community accompaniment, and preventive conflict management.",
"Action/Intervention": "Identify institutional responsibilities, articulation points, and operational gaps between the Escazú implementation Roadmap and the Nature Pledge governance framework; design the national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders, including institutional architecture, complaint pathways, activation criteria, protection measures, and inter-institutional coordination, based on Article 9 of the Escazú Agreement and current national regulations; integrate Escazú principles on access to environmental information into national information and monitoring systems, ensuring coherence with Target 25 and ANTAI's role; develop operational protocols to guarantee effective public participation and access to environmental justice in Nature Pledge implementation, prioritizing territories with high socio-environmental conflict; define indicators aligned with the national system for monitoring adaptation, loss, and damage; implement the national mechanism for protection of environmental defenders in prioritized territories and articulate it with the community resilience observatories in Target 27; implement territorial mechanisms for access to information, participation, and environmental justice through public environmental-information platforms, territorial outreach and participation events, and technical and legal accompaniment schemes for communities and vulnerable groups; incorporate mandatory criteria of equitable representation and a gender approach into regulations, terms of reference, and designation mechanisms of Nature Pledge decision-making spaces and apply them at national and territorial levels; consolidate local capacities for mediation, community accompaniment, and preventive management of conflicts linked to environmental projects.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Environmental governance, access to environmental information, public participation, environmental justice, protection of environmental defenders, national information and monitoring systems, Nature Pledge decision-making spaces, prioritized territories with high socio-environmental conflict, and implementation of environmental projects.",
"Target Audience": "National institutions responsible for the Escazú Agreement Roadmap and Nature Pledge governance framework; ANTAI; institutions involved in the protection of environmental defenders; Nature Pledge decision-making spaces at national and territorial levels; communities and vulnerable groups in prioritized territories; environmental defenders; and local actors involved in mediation, accompaniment, and conflict prevention.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Operational coherence between the Escazú implementation Roadmap and the Nature Pledge governance framework; a defined and effectively operating national mechanism for the protection of environmental defenders in prioritized territories; integration of access-to-information principles into national information and monitoring systems; operational protocols and territorial mechanisms in place for effective public participation and access to environmental justice; indicators established for access to information, participation, protection of defenders, and gender equity; equitable representation and gender approach applied in Nature Pledge decision-making spaces; and strengthened local capacities for mediation, accompaniment, and preventive conflict management linked to environmental projects."
panama_HR_30:
"Goal/Purpose": "Finalize, adopt, submit, approve, promulgate, regulate, monitor, and coordinate the Climate Change and Green Transition Framework Law, the Nature Pledge, and related regulatory and governance instruments at the national level.",
"Action/Intervention": "Finalize the technical, inter-institutional, and participatory consultation process of the draft Climate Change and Green Transition Framework Law; formally adopt the Nature Pledge through an administrative instrument establishing its national-level implementation; develop, integrate, and operationalize a Nature Pledge monitoring module in the National Climate Transparency Platform to ensure traceability of targets, indicators, and progress by implementation phase, articulated with structural targets and the regulatory implementation package of the Pact; obtain political endorsement from the Executive Branch (Ministry of the Presidency, Cabinet Council) for the regulatory package; formally submit to the National Assembly the draft Framework Law, the Environmental Non-regression Law, and provisions on the Pact and unified governance; drive legislative approval and promulgation of the Framework Law; develop and approve priority regulations of the Framework Law focused on planning instruments, information and monitoring systems, and inter-institutional coordination mechanisms; establish the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee as a technical and participatory body with multi-sectoral representation and clear advisory, follow-up, and technical coherence functions.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate change, green transition, nature, biodiversity, land, national governance, legislation, regulation, planning, monitoring, and inter-institutional coordination.",
"Target Audience": "Executive Branch institutions including the Ministry of the Presidency and Cabinet Council; the National Assembly; inter-institutional actors; participatory stakeholders; and the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "The draft Framework Law consultation process is finalized; the Nature Pledge is formally adopted through an administrative instrument; a Nature Pledge monitoring module is operational in the National Climate Transparency Platform with traceability of targets, indicators, and progress by implementation phase; political endorsement of the regulatory package is obtained from the Executive Branch; the draft Framework Law, Environmental Non-regression Law, and provisions on the Pact and unified governance are formally submitted to the National Assembly; the Framework Law is legislatively approved and promulgated; priority regulations are developed and approved; and the National Climate, Biodiversity, and Land Committee is established."

panama_PEG_29:
"Goal/Purpose": "Develop a law and comprehensive strategy for the green transition and for facing climate change by 2050, so that Panama's economy and society take the necessary measures to prosper despite the climate crisis, biodiversity loss, desertification, and pollution.",
"Action/Intervention": "Create a national cabinet with representatives from State entities to local authorities for management and planning of actions and for promoting a joint implementation and investment framework at national and regional level; carry out vulnerability assessments of critical infrastructure such as ports, transport and energy systems; systematize, improve, and modernize measurement, reporting, and verification processes for data and information related to the green transition and climate action, ensuring access and availability for all Panamanians and prioritizing scientific data for adaptation measures; establish a national climate and environmental early-warning system focused on communities in flood-, drought-, extreme temperature-, and coastal-risk areas, reaching 80% of at-risk communities, accompanied by continuous training in disaster risk reduction; establish community resilience centers in each region with authorities and local partners; restore degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula; adopt international standards for transparent reporting of climate-risk management in the financial and business sectors; regulate and capitalize the National Adaptation Fund to finance community resilience and preparedness initiatives; back and finance research initiatives in restoration, conservation, climate change, sustainable agriculture, clean energy, reduction of plastic use, and biodiversity protection.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Panama at national and regional level; critical infrastructure sectors including ports, transport and energy systems; communities in areas prone to floods, droughts, extreme temperature rises, and coastal zones; each region of the country; degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula; financial and business sectors; research areas related to restoration, conservation, climate change, sustainable agriculture, clean energy, plastic reduction, and biodiversity protection.",
"Target Audience": "State entities, local authorities, national and regional institutions, communities at risk from climate impacts, all Panamanians, authorities and local partners, financial and business sectors, and research initiatives.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A law and comprehensive strategy for the green transition and climate action by 2050; a functioning national cabinet for coordinated management, planning, implementation, and investment; vulnerability assessments of critical infrastructure completed; improved and modernized measurement, reporting, and verification systems with accessible information and planning instruments; a national climate and environmental early-warning system reaching 80% of at-risk communities and supported by continuous disaster risk reduction training; community resilience centers established in each region; restored degraded ecosystems and key watersheds in the Azuero Peninsula to guarantee human consumption, agriculture, health, and regional development; adoption of international standards for transparent climate-risk reporting in financial and business sectors; a regulated and capitalized National Adaptation Fund financing community initiatives; and financed research supporting innovation in the specified areas."
panama_PEG_30:
"Goal/Purpose": "Protect nature through a unified international commitment presented to the UN; exchange knowledge and sustainable practices and execute joint actions for the benefit of Mother Earth; ensure all sectors of society contribute to discussion on the country's green and blue future integrating sociocultural development with environmental sustainability; face common environmental and climate challenges through international collaboration; decarbonize international maritime and air transport; conserve marine biodiversity in international waters; significantly reduce the production and consumption of single-use plastics and promote sustainable alternatives; protect key ecosystems and ensure marine conservation and resource sustainability in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor (CMAR).",
"Action/Intervention": "Present to the UN a unified international commitment for the protection of nature ('Nature Pledge') with climate, biodiversity, and desertification targets; promote inter-territorial and intercultural alliances among local communities, civil society, indigenous peoples, faith groups, and other key actors; lead participatory national processes involving all sectors of society; promote collaborations on environmental and climate issues with MERCOSUR countries, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and other like-minded nations; form a high-level commission to drive national and global measures for decarbonizing international maritime and air transport; ratify the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ); reaffirm and adopt the Global Plastics Treaty; work with neighboring countries to ensure effective and coordinated management of the Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor (CMAR).",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Nature protection; climate, biodiversity, and desertification; local and national societal processes; environmental and climate cooperation; international maritime and air transport; marine biodiversity in international waters; plastics production and consumption; Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor (CMAR) and key marine ecosystems.",
"Target Audience": "The UN; Panama; local communities; civil society; indigenous peoples; faith groups; other key actors; all sectors of society; MERCOSUR countries; Small Island Developing States (SIDS); other like-minded nations; national and global decision-makers involved in maritime and air transport; neighboring countries.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Panama becomes the first country in the world to present a unified international commitment for nature protection to the UN; knowledge and sustainable practices are exchanged and joint actions are executed; all sectors of society contribute to discussion on the country's green and blue future; countries facing common challenges share experiences and develop joint strategies; national and global measures for decarbonizing international maritime and air transport are driven; commitment to conservation of marine biodiversity in international waters is cemented through ratification of the High Seas Treaty; production and consumption of single-use plastics are significantly reduced and sustainable alternatives are promoted; marine conservation, resource sustainability, and protection of key ecosystems in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Marine Corridor are strengthened."

panama_PNSH_1:
"Goal/Purpose": "To ensure that every person in this country has sustained access to quality water and basic sanitation, sufficiently safe to lead a dignified, clean, healthy, and productive life.",
"Action/Intervention": "Progressively expand the coverage of water and sanitation services at the national level and eliminate inequalities in access in an inclusive and equitable manner, in accordance with users' needs.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Water and sanitation services at the national level.",
"Target Audience": "Every person in this country; users of water and sanitation services.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Universal access to quality water and sanitation services, with expanded national coverage and elimination of inequalities in access."
panama_PNSH_2:
"Goal/Purpose": "Improve the efficiency of drinking water and sanitation services by optimizing existing infrastructure, improving treatment plant operations, improving rural water systems, and reinforcing, improving, and optimizing sanitary sewer services.",
"Action/Intervention": "Execute 174 projects; optimize existing infrastructure; make the operation of treatment plants more efficient; improve rural water systems in their operation and distribution of water directly to households; reinforce, improve, and optimize sanitary sewer services; improve existing drinking water and sewer systems; optimize water consumption through micro- and macro-metering; implement strategies for leak reduction.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Drinking water and sanitation services, including drinking water systems, treatment plants, rural water systems, and sanitary sewer services.",
"Target Audience": "Around 1 million people across the country who will benefit from the projects.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Around 1 million people across the country will benefit through the execution of 174 projects, addressing the most critical problems in the provision of drinking water and sanitation services."
panama_PNSH_3:
"Goal/Purpose": "Increase coverage of drinking water services by expanding water supply coverage at the urban and rural levels in communities where service is deficient.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out studies and corresponding designs, and construct and/or expand treatment plants, rural water systems, wells, water systems, conveyance lines, and supply systems; execute 136 construction and/or expansion projects for new treatment plants, rural water systems, and wells between 2015 and 2020.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Drinking water supply services in urban, rural, peri-urban, and rural and indigenous areas.",
"Target Audience": "Communities where drinking water service is deficient, including urban and rural populations, rural communities transitioning into peri-urban centers, and populations in rural and indigenous areas.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "By 2020, drinking water supply coverage reaches 98% of the urban population and 70% of rural and indigenous areas."
panama_PNSH_4:
"Goal/Purpose": "To provide all households with basic sanitation conditions.",

"Ecosystem/Area": "Sanitation services and sanitary sewer systems in cities and across the country.",
"Target Audience": "All households.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Increased sanitation services, with all households provided with basic sanitation conditions and latrines eliminated across the country."
panama_PNSH_5:

"Ecosystem/Area": "Water and sanitation systems at the national level.",
"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified in the target.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Evaluation of the behavior of supply, demand, and water-supply efficiency, and development of 12 projects under water and sanitation studies and water and sanitation plans."

"Goal/Purpose": "Management of water-resource availability.",

panama_PNSH_8:
"Goal/Purpose": "To organize freshwater use and consumption, make demand more efficient through technological tools, and monitor compliance.",
"Action/Intervention": "Organizing user demand; adopting technological tools and more efficient water-use systems; monitoring compliance; carrying out studies for the use of treated wastewater in cities; implementing projects for the use of treated wastewater in cities; improving irrigation system technology; developing new options for reserving water; improving irrigation distribution systems.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Freshwater demand management, urban water use, and irrigation systems.",
"Target Audience": "Water users.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "More efficient water demand and consumption management; use of treated wastewater in cities; improved irrigation technology and distribution systems; development of new water reservation options; 24 projects identified in the thematic areas of user demand organization, adoption of new technologies and more efficient water-use systems, and improvements to irrigation distribution systems."
panama_PNSH_9:
"Goal/Purpose": "Increase the availability of freshwater by expanding water-resource availability and storage capacity to meet current and future needs, and prevent future shortages caused by the effects of an unpredictable climate.",
"Action/Intervention": "Carry out studies and research to evaluate and demonstrate the feasibility of increasing water availability; construct infrastructure to conserve water, including multipurpose reservoirs and accelerated rainwater harvesting in the metropolitan area and provincial capitals; convert reservoirs currently used exclusively for energy into multipurpose reservoirs; establish multipurpose reservoirs in the Indio, Santa María, La Villa, Perales, Parita, Oria, and Ocú rivers; implement rainwater harvesting projects; initiate social, environmental, and economic studies and technical designs for a Bayano water treatment plant; use rainwater harvesting, cloud seeding, and water reserves for agriculture.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Freshwater resources and water infrastructure in the metropolitan area, provincial capitals, the eastern sector of the province of Panama, and the Indio, Santa María, La Villa, Perales, Parita, Oria, and Ocú rivers.",
"Target Audience": "Population in the eastern sector of the province of Panama; users with needs for drinking water consumption, food production, energy generation, industry, transport, recreation, ecosystems, agriculture, new uses, and urban growth.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Increased freshwater availability and water storage capacity; water conserved through reservoirs and rainwater harvesting; support for current and future needs for drinking water, food production, energy generation, industry, transport, recreation, ecosystems, agriculture, new uses, and urban growth; prevention of future water shortages caused by an unpredictable climate."
panama_PNSH_10:
"Goal/Purpose": "Preventive management of water-related risks; to mitigate impacts and increase the resilience of people and infrastructure to extreme events.",

"Ecosystem/Area": "Water management; water-related risks.",
"Target Audience": "Decision-makers in water management; people and infrastructure.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Improved capacity for decision-making in water management, mitigation of impacts, and increased resilience of people and infrastructure to extreme events."
panama_PNSH_11:
"Goal/Purpose": "To mitigate the impacts of climate events, prevent them from becoming disasters, reduce the vulnerability of people and public and private water and sanitation infrastructure, and thereby maintain the country's growth levels and protect its natural resources, including water.",
"Action/Intervention": "Diagnosis of the risk situation; implementation of the National Program for Hydrological Extremes Management; adaptation and mitigation plans, including climate change; dredging and channeling of rivers; open and underground river drainage in urban areas; developing tools to identify risks, reduce their impacts, prepare for emergencies, financially protect investments, and plan for the recovery and restoration of infrastructure.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Risk management in the water and sanitation sector, including rivers and urban drainage areas.",
"Target Audience": "People; public and private water and sanitation infrastructure.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Reduced impacts of climate events, prevention of disasters, reduced vulnerability of people and water and sanitation infrastructure, maintenance of the country's growth levels, protection of natural resources including water, and improved recovery and restoration planning for infrastructure."
panama_PNSH_12:
"Goal/Purpose": "Monitor climate events and their effects and install early-warning systems, with attention to disasters and extreme climate events.",
"Action/Intervention": "Invest in the purchase, installation, operation, and replacement of instruments necessary to monitor climate events and their effects; implement ten programmed projects; install early-warning systems; establish an early-warning system for floods and landslides in watersheds; develop an agroclimatic system for the agricultural sector; strengthen SINAPROC's Desinventar platform; install an early-warning system in schools; determine a vulnerability index and define government action thresholds for extreme events; purchase and operate hydrometeorological stations for the agricultural sector; continue operating SINAPROC's tide-monitoring system; install tide gauges; install sensors for electrical discharges; acquire a satellite-image reception station.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Climate risk monitoring and early warning; watersheds; agricultural sector; schools; tide/coastal monitoring.",
"Target Audience": "SINAPROC; the agricultural sector; schools; government.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Operational monitoring instruments and systems for climate events and their effects, including early-warning systems for floods, landslides, schools, and extreme events; a strengthened Desinventar platform; a developed agroclimatic system; a determined vulnerability index and defined government action thresholds; continued tide monitoring; and installed tide gauges, electrical discharge sensors, hydrometeorological stations, and a satellite-image reception station."
panama_PNSH_13:

"Ecosystem/Area": "Water; water governance; water management.",
"Target Audience": "Institutions with a mandate related to water; society; all water users.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "A level of satisfaction adequate to the needs of all water users."

"Target Audience": "Water users; watershed committees; mediators; local authorities; institutions.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Resolved conflicts over access to water, prevention of future water-resource conflicts, and strengthened consultation, participation, and conflict-resolution capacity during the Plan's validity."

"Target Audience": "Not explicitly specified in the target.",

panama_PNSH_16:

"Ecosystem/Area": "Water resource management and integrated water governance.",
"Target Audience": "Current staff and new staff involved in implementing the PNSH.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Implementation of the PNSH through strengthened institutional capacity across the four identified areas."
panama_PNSH_17:

"Action/Intervention": "Implement 12 planned investment projects, including short-term investments, organized into two lines of action: training for better water use; research for better water management; and planning and training of professionals in water (identification of technical careers), within the framework of the National Strategic Plan for Science, Technology, and Innovation coordinated by SENACYT.",
"Ecosystem/Area": "Water resources; use, protection, conservation, and management of water.",
"Target Audience": "Professionals in water.",
"Expected Impact/Outcome": "Strengthened education, capacity-building, and information on water use, protection, and conservation; better water use; better water management; and planning and training of water professionals."
